a.xlink:title: A disabled glyph recedes past the quiet level, whatever the family.
WCAG contrast ratio between two opaque colors, from 1.0 to 21.0.
The harder of two surfaces to keep an ink legible on.
The ink a disabled glyph is painted with, given the quiet level.
Fallback for an application color role when the active theme does not define one.
Applies an emphasis level to an already-hued glyph color.
Icon ink for a neutral glyph, given the palette it is drawn from.
Mixes two colors, amount = 0 returning color and 1 returning target.
Whether hue belongs to the band the Positive or Negative family owns.
Pushes color away from background until it reaches minRatio.
WCAG relative luminance of an opaque color.
A neutral glyph at the family's primary level, for the surface's primary action.
A dimmed neutral glyph, for a control that labels rather than acts.
Resolves the concrete color for an icon mode.
